blindSummary:
This state/province is the site of the most severe single incident in the country's trans-violence series: in June 2025, in a city here, a hooded gunman shot a transgender rights activist and radio commentator several times at the acupuncture clinic she owned, killing her; police explicitly investigated whether her history of activism was connected. An international human-rights organisation called it an "apparent targeted killing." The national human-rights commission publicly condemned the killing as "marked by cruelty and impunity" — the strongest official language in the record, naming the victim specifically.

No protective ordinance, institutional counterweight, or positive enforcement response (arrest of the actual gunman) is documented. The "impunity" framing from the commission is itself the damning signal the scoring rules treat as a large negative factor.

Net effect: a large negative deviation from the national baseline. This is the only unit where the violence is both targeted at trans-specificity and explicitly flagged as unaddressed by the official body. Compare the national capital district, which carries two killings but pairs them with arrests and the country's strongest protective ordinances; compare a neighbouring state/province, where a single killing drew a homicide investigation within days.
